messages:
Alice Chen: Quick question — canary + header override + session cookie sticky behavior seems ambiguous. If path /api/v2 matches a weighted route and we also have X-Canary: beta header, and session cookie points to original cohort, which wins? Observed case where header took precedence but the UI implies session affinity should. Is that intended? :thinking_face:
Ben Ortiz: We designed header overrides to be highest priority for experiments so integrators can force a model variant. But that should be opt-in. Which service/route is this?
Alice Chen: service=api-gateway, route id=svc-472, config attached below. Repro: set cookie cohort=A then send header X-Canary=beta and you get beta even after set-cookie.
Carla Singh: That's consistent with current impl: route evaluation order = exact path -> header rules -> weight splits -> cookie stickiness. Maybe we need path/weight precedence doc. But would be good to confirm if cookie stickiness should outrank header override for long-running sessions.
Dinesh Patel: For safety, we treat headers as explicit developer intent, so they override stickiness. But that breaks rollout UX for end-users. We should add a 'sticky_override: false' flag so teams can opt out of header forcing.
Eva Morales: Telemetry question: when header overrides a bucket, how do we attribute metrics? We should tag requests with origin: header|cookie|default so dashboards show true exposure.
Ben Ortiz: Agreed. Also sampling: current telemetry samples 0.1% for traces; for canary we want deterministic sampling for header-forced requests. Maybe set sample_rate=1 for any forced header so we always get traces.
Carla Singh: Proposed config snippet:
```
routes:
  - match: path_prefix: /api/v2
    experiments:
      - id: canary-2026-03
        strategy: weighted
        weights: {stable: 90, beta: 10}
        header_override: true
        sticky_override: false
```
Alice Chen: Nice. UX ask: console should show a banner when header_override=true that reads 'Certain requests may bypass session affinity'. Also per-route telemetry breakdown with 'origin' tag.
DeployBot: deploy requested by Carla Singh for svc-472/canary-2026-03 — started (hash: f9a2b3). :rocket:
Dinesh Patel: If we change default sticky_override we need migration plan. Some customers rely on header forcing in tests. Maybe make it per-tenant flag.
Ben Ortiz: +1 on per-tenant. Also add a warning in rollout UI when you enable header_override.
Eva Morales: I'll add metrics:canary.origin and adjust dashboards. Also will add a short eval to detect coverage gaps if header-forced traffic isn't instrumented.
Alice Chen: Thanks — can someone file a tiny RFC? I'll gather notes. @Carla @Dinesh
Carla Singh: I'll draft RFC and ping infra for migration notes.
Ben Ortiz: I'll update router eval order doc and add tests.
Alice Chen: Awesome. End of thread.
